question.text:
CASE STUDY: Priya, aged 32, is an IT professional in Bengaluru earning a monthly salary of Rs. 1,20,000. After monthly expenses of Rs. 60,000 and existing EMIs of Rs. 20,000, she has Rs. 40,000 available for investment. She has the following financial goals: (1) Build an emergency fund of Rs. 3,60,000 (6 months' expenses) -- needed within 1 year; (2) Save for her 3-year-old daughter Ananya's higher education (current cost Rs. 25,00,000) -- needed in 15 years; (3) Build a retirement corpus -- she plans to retire at age 60 (28 years away); (4) Down payment of Rs. 15,00,000 for a house -- needed in 5 years. She currently has Rs. 2,00,000 in a savings account and no other investments. She is comfortable with moderate market fluctuations but panics during sharp market corrections.
Question 1: Using the commonly applied time-horizon buckets of short-term (up to 3 years), medium-term (3 to 7 years), and long-term (more than 7 years), which of the following correctly classifies Priya's financial goals?

answer.text: Emergency fund: Short-term; House down payment: Medium-term; Child's education: Long-term; Retirement: Long-term
Emergency fund: Short-term; House down payment: Short-term; Child's education: Medium-term; Retirement: Long-term
Emergency fund: Immediate; House down payment: Medium-term; Child's education: Medium-term; Retirement: Long-term
Emergency fund: Short-term; House down payment: Long-term; Child's education: Long-term; Retirement: Long-term

explanation.text: The Logic: Applying the stem's stated buckets — short-term (up to 3 years), medium-term (3 to 7 years), long-term (more than 7 years) — Priya's goals map as follows: emergency fund in 1 year is short-term; house down payment in 5 years is medium-term (5 falls inside 3 to 7); daughter's education in 15 years and retirement in 28 years are both long-term (both exceed 7). Only option A reflects this mapping for every goal. The Trap: Option B incorrectly drops the 5-year house goal into short-term and the 15-year education goal into medium-term. Option C invents an "Immediate" bucket not present in the stem. Option D pushes the 5-year house goal into long-term. In the original ambiguous wording, candidates could defend several mappings because the boundary values were not stated; the audit flagged that the 0/3/7-year cut-offs were not explicit in the workbook pages checked. Note: The original stem (NISM Series V-A workbook, p.14-17) referred to "short/medium/long-term goal classification" but did not state the exact 0-3, 3-7, 7-plus year boundaries on the pages cited. The stem has been tightened to declare those boundaries explicitly, so the keyed answer is now uniquely determined by the stem's own definitions rather than by an unstated convention.
